clue.text: Presumption of worth still being bandied about

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled word for still is wrapped around the word for worth
bandied means tossed to and fro, so the letters of the word for still are jumbled

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'yet to come'
worth means merit

explanation.surface: Someone's value is still being argued over, and that seems presumptuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandied' jumbles the word for still into TEY, which 'about' then wraps round; 'being' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, the same as presumption or cheek.

clue.text: Headgear which needs some work put in

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the word for which

parts.note: that can stand in for which as a relative pronoun
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hat that needs some work done to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat is a form of formal headgear.

clue.text: Capital housing source of laid paper

indicators.note: housing means holding inside

parts.note: Manila is the capital of the Philippines

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A capital city houses the source of laid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla is a strong brown paper used for envelopes and folders.

clue.text: Decrepit couple going after sheep

indicators.note: going after means placed after the sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to shackle is to couple or chain together

explanation.surface: A pair chases after some sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle means rickety and falling apart, like a decrepit shed.

clue.text: Needle (key) match — eke it out …

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A key match is stretched out by needle.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but is only punctuation here.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone and to tease or mock them mean the same thing.

clue.text: Put on the way over the hill

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street, a way
over the hill is an idiom for old, aged

explanation.surface: Someone was put on the road over the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged is put on, mounted as a production.

clue.text: … national hero has to blow the whistle

explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is Switzerland's hero, and to inform on someone is to grass them up.

clue.text: Bomb posing danger out east

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb poses danger in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DANGER into GRENAD; 'posing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb.

clue.text: Colouring — I agree, half of it's useless to go outside

indicators.note: the word for useless goes around the rest

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless or broken
yes means I agree

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word it is its second letter

parts.note: the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: Agreeing that half of this colouring is useless goes outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go outside' wraps the useless word round the agreement plus T, the second half of 'it'; DUFF is British slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is a substance that gives colour, a dye.

clue.text: Bird shut up in prison

definitions.meaning: a female swan is called by this name
to confine someone, as in an enclosure or penitentiary

explanation.definitionFit: A female swan bears this name, and the verb means to confine or coop up.

clue.text: Convince with pretence

definitions.meaning: to cause someone to believe something

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to cause someone to believe, and as a hyphenated noun it means fantasy or pretending.

clue.text: Misuse pubs with not unusual arrogance

indicators.note: unusual signals an odd arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Misusing pubs is an all-too-common form of arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unusual' tempts as a phrase meaning common, but 'not' is fodder and 'unusual' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumptiousness is self-assertive conceit, arrogance.

clue.text: Without exception, best-ever article is penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the article sits inside the word for best-ever

parts.note: an all-time record is the best ever
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Every single time, the finest article ever is written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'written', but here it means shut in, as an animal is penned.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for always, constantly, with no exception.

clue.text: Players can always see through their leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the four preceding words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Actors can always see through things, it is claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its set of players or actors.

clue.text: Stop writer sending up sick conductor

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A conductor stops a writer mocking him because he is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Barbirolli was an English conductor of the Hallé Orchestra; Biro is the British name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbirolli was a celebrated orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Awkward cowboy drops end of lasso, ending in failure

indicators.note: drops means loses, so a letter is removed from the word for cowboy

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy

indicators.note: the end of lasso is its last letter
ending in picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A clumsy cowboy loses hold of the end of his lasso and fails.
explanation.walkthrough: GAUCHO loses O (the end of lasso) and takes E, the end of failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche, from French for left, means socially awkward or clumsy.

clue.text: One's often bagged — in more ways than one

definitions.text: One's often bagged — in more ways than one

parts.words: One's often bagged — in more ways than one
parts.note: one sense is the dried leaves sold in small sachets for brewing; the other is cockney rhyming slang for a thief, who is often caught, or bagged

explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang this phrase means thief, and thieves get bagged (arrested); the same leaves come in bags for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea comes in bags, and as rhyming slang for thief the phrase names someone often caught.

clue.text: Size of paper the panel got wrong

indicators.note: got wrong signals the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The panel got the paper size wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant is a traditional large paper size.

clue.text: Siren — there are legends attached to flowers round neck

parts.note: lore is a body of legends and traditions
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Legends tell of a siren wearing a garland of flowers round her neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the siren of German legend who lured Rhine boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: How head of state appears, say, during assembly

indicators.note: during means inside the word for assembly

parts.note: a rally is a mass assembly
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: How a monarch looks, for instance, at a mass meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of state such as a king appears in a royal, stately manner.

clue.text: Courses dished up in bistro

indicators.note: dished up suggests served in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Courses served in a small restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are the paths or courses that bodies follow around a planet or star.

clue.text: Foodstuff obtained from a firm I butter up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole string is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
taken as written
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A food got from a company that flatters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A + CO + I + PAT, giving TAPIOCA; 'butter up' looks like flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy food made from cassava root.

clue.text: Touch end of left arm

indicators.note: the end of left is its last letter

parts.note: a rifle is a firearm

explanation.surface: Touching the end of the left arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch and a trifle both mean a small amount, as in 'a trifle sad'.

clue.text: Pressure applied to mature servant

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on a servant to grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young attendant or boy servant.

clue.text: Visiting island to row river — it provides a long descent

indicators.note: the row visits, or goes into, the island

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island
a scrap is a fight or row

explanation.surface: Someone visits an island to row on its river, which has a long descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' tempts as part of the definition, but it is the container signal; Skye is an island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building gives a long drop from top to street.

clue.text: Humdinger turned up in gambling centre

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read backwards

parts.note: a oner is British slang for something outstanding, a humdinger

explanation.surface: Something remarkable turned up in a gambling town.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno, Nevada, is a gambling city.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno in Nevada is famous for its casinos.

clue.text: Everyone's fit to make an ironic objection

parts.note: everyone is all
fit means in good health, very well

explanation.surface: Everyone being fit is grounds for a wry complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to grant a point grudgingly before objecting, as in 'that's fine, but...'.

clue.text: Away from unopened shed

indicators.note: unopened means without the first letter

parts.note: to doff is to shed or take ... clothing

explanation.surface: A shed that's never been opened stands apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Off means away from, as in 'keep off the grass'.

clue.text: Gigolo featured in rhyme

parts.note: a young kept lover whose two-word name contains a rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: The two words of this name for a young male lover rhyme with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang name for a young man kept as a lover by an older woman.

clue.text: Guess the cost of vehicle I am seated inside

indicators.note: seated inside means placed within the vehicle

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, a station wagon
I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: Work out what it costs for a car with me sitting in it.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge an approximate price or value.
